_readme: Approved variant questions for Chapters 2 to 9 (one extra per section, so each section has two and students get different questions). Options are kept close in length so the longest option is not a giveaway; the correct option is not systematically longer.

quizzes.question: According to this section, what is money defined by, rather than by what it is made of?
options: The weight and rarity of the material itself
The job it does and people's shared agreement
The official body that first approved its use

quizzes.question: Why did even non-smokers accept cigarettes in a prison economy?
options: They were told to by the prison guards and staff
They were the only item the prison shop sold
They knew someone else would accept them too

quizzes.question: What does money's job as a 'unit of account' let people do?
options: Price and compare very different things
Prove who owns a particular coin or note
Hold wealth safely until a later date

quizzes.question: What does the section name as gold's one real weakness as money?
options: It rots quickly if it is not kept dry and cool
It cannot be split into smaller standard units
A large amount is heavy and hard to move around

quizzes.question: An early banknote that could be swapped for gold is an example of which kind of money?
options: Representative money, a claim on gold
Commodity money, valuable in itself
Fiat money, backed only by decree

quizzes.question: According to this section, what does money that loses value quickly push people toward?
options: Saving much more to wait for better prices
Spending straight away instead of saving
Swapping everything they own for cattle

quizzes.question: What does the section say usually frustrates people during the Barter Game?
options: The person who wants your item lacks what you want
Nobody at all wants any of the things people brought
Everyone refuses to take part in any kind of trade

quizzes.question: Why does barter become nearly impossible in a town of ten thousand people?
options: Large towns do not have enough spare food to trade
A perfect match of wants almost never comes up
Traders in big towns refuse to deal with strangers

quizzes.question: What does the word 'salary' point back to, according to this section?
options: Medieval farmers being paid in sacks of grain
Sailors being paid in shells at the harbour
Roman soldiers being paid partly in salt rations

quizzes.question: What did the stamp on a coin let two strangers do?
options: Prove that the metal was mined in their own town
Trust its weight and purity without testing it
Swap the coin for gold at any bank they liked

quizzes.question: Which limit on creating money disappeared once the link to gold was cut?
options: Needing shops to give their permission first
Needing every note to be printed at a mint
Needing real gold to back any new money printed

quizzes.question: What does a card payment depend on, according to this section?
options: The bank's systems and permission both working
A government office signing off on each purchase
The shop keeping enough cash in its till all day

quizzes.question: What is the key difference between Bitcoin-style digital money and bank digital money?
options: It exists only as paper certificates kept in a vault
One trusted bank still holds everybody's balance
No single institution keeps the official record

quizzes.question: According to this section, what does the worth of a rand note rest on?
options: Trust that people will keep on accepting it as money
The amount of gold stored in the central bank
The cost of the paper and ink used to print it

quizzes.question: How did other countries end up in the fiat system after 1971?
options: Each one held a vote to leave the gold standard
Their currencies were pegged to the US dollar
The United States ordered them to make the switch

quizzes.question: In the layered picture of the fiat system, who can create the base currency?
options: The central bank, at the very top
Commercial banks with branches
Ordinary users who earn and save

quizzes.question: Who tends to gain when a central bank lowers interest rates, according to this section?
options: Older savers who rely on interest from banks
Borrowers and people who already own assets
People who keep all of their money as cash notes

quizzes.question: What detail about the lending chain surprises most people, according to this section?
options: One bank is secretly printing all the extra money
The government approves every single loan by hand
Every bank simply follows a normal, legal process

quizzes.question: In the Cantillon example, who gets to spend at the old, lower prices?
options: The worker whose raise comes through last
Whoever is handed the new money first of all
Every person in the economy at the same time

quizzes.question: What would a CBDC remove from between a person and the central bank?
options: The shop that accepts the payment
The paper note that is handed over
The commercial bank in the middle

quizzes.question: What two ways of looking does this chapter ask you to hold together?
options: Understanding a system and judging its effects
Studying the past and then predicting the future
Reading the text and then doing the activities

quizzes.question: According to this section, what can inflation always be traced back to?
options: Bad weather that damages harvests each year
Shops deciding together to put their prices up
An identifiable cause, such as money creation

quizzes.question: At 10% a year, roughly what would the R100 basket cost after ten years?
options: About R259
About R200
About R180

quizzes.question: Besides growing debt, what second problem does this section name?
options: A shortage of bank branches in the small towns
A widening gap between asset holders and others
A drop in the number of people who have jobs

quizzes.question: What does the section say working harder cannot fix?
options: A problem built into the money itself
A lack of skills needed for a better job
A shortage of jobs in your own area

quizzes.question: What is the comparison between the two groups really about, in this section?
options: Whether people earn more than ten thousand a month
Whether wealth sits in assets or in wages and cash
Whether people live in big cities or in villages

quizzes.question: Which option for a government covers a debt gap but also feeds inflation?
options: Raising taxes on shops, traders and workers
Cutting spending on public services and grants
Creating more currency to help cover the gap

quizzes.question: What did the community in this section ask about money?
options: Whether banks could be made to lend much more
Whether money could work without one controller
Whether gold could be brought back by a new law

quizzes.question: How was the Cypherpunks' approach different from earlier attempts to fix money?
options: They asked central banks to change their policies
They wrote new laws to limit what banks could do
They built systems needing no trusted institution

quizzes.question: What test does the section suggest for spotting a decentralized system?
options: Could one party alone block someone from using it?
Does it have a website and a customer service line?
Is it older than the banks it is meant to replace?

quizzes.question: Why does physical cash not have a double-spend problem?
options: Every note carries a different serial number
Banks check each note before it is spent
Handing it over means you no longer have it

quizzes.question: What was happening in the world when the Bitcoin whitepaper appeared in late 2008?
options: A financial crisis that tested trust in banks
A boom in the price of gold and of silver coins
A new law that made bank cards the only money

quizzes.question: What does Bitcoin do that earlier digital cash systems did not do?
options: Reduces the record-keepers to one trusted party
Maximises the number of record-keepers it uses
Lets one company approve each transaction

quizzes.question: What is the key asymmetry behind Proof-of-Work?
options: Hard and costly to produce, but easy to check
Easy to produce, but very hard to check
Costly for honest miners but free for cheaters

quizzes.question: What happens if miners enforce rules that full nodes and users reject?
options: The new rules take effect for the whole network
Their blocks are refused, so their power is wasted
Developers are forced to update all the software

quizzes.question: Which chapter's list of money properties does this section test Bitcoin against?
options: Chapter 4
Chapter 5
Chapter 2

quizzes.question: Why is Bitcoin unusual in the history of money, according to this section?
options: Its properties formed by accident over centuries
Its properties were chosen deliberately in advance
Its properties were set by a central bank in 2009

quizzes.question: What is the smallest unit of bitcoin mentioned in this section?
options: A millibitcoin, 0.001 BTC
A centibitcoin, 0.01 BTC
A satoshi, 0.00000001 BTC

quizzes.question: Why is there no customer service line that can reverse a Bitcoin mistake?
options: No single party can override the whole system
Banks are not allowed to hold any bitcoin at all
The software deletes the record after a few days

quizzes.question: What kind of skills does this chapter shift towards?
options: Historical ones, such as studying old coins
Technical ones, such as writing mining code
Practical ones, such as setting up a wallet

quizzes.question: Which three ways of acquiring bitcoin does this section list?
options: Trading in person, trading online, or an exchange
Mining at home, borrowing it, or taking a bank loan
Gifts only, from family, friends or an employer

quizzes.question: What does physical peer-to-peer trading not require, according to this section?
options: A working Lightning or on-chain wallet to use
A bank account or ID check with a far-off company
Someone nearby who is willing to trade with you

quizzes.question: What do online peer-to-peer platforms use to protect both sides of a trade?
options: Escrow services
Bank guarantees
Paper contracts

quizzes.question: On a centralized exchange, who holds your bitcoin until you withdraw it?
options: You do, in your own private wallet
The exchange does, on your behalf
Your bank does, in your own account

quizzes.question: What does a Bitcoin wallet actually hold?
options: Small amounts of bitcoin stored on the phone
Copies of every transaction on the blockchain
The keys that prove you control your bitcoin

quizzes.question: What is the cost of a self-custodial wallet, compared with a custodial one?
options: A company can freeze your account at will
Nobody can help you recover a lost private key
You must trust a firm not to go out of business

quizzes.question: Which kind of wallet suits everyday spending, such as a taxi fare?
options: An on-chain wallet
A paper wallet
A Lightning wallet

quizzes.question: What does closed-source wallet software prevent people from doing?
options: Checking for themselves what the code does
Sending any bitcoin at all to other wallets
Using the wallet on more than one phone or tablet

quizzes.question: What is the recovery phrase described as in this section?
options: A password that support staff can reset
A receipt that proves you bought bitcoin
The master key to all of your funds

quizzes.question: What does the section say you should do before confirming a send?
options: Double-check the address
Phone your bank and ask
Wait a full day first

quizzes.question: How does the section describe bitcoin's price in the short term?
options: Steady, so it carries no risk at all
Volatile, so it suits the long term
Fixed by the central bank each month

quizzes.question: What does 'Don't Trust, Verify' encourage you to do, as the section describes it?
options: Check claims for yourself, using block explorers
Believe the course because it was written for you
Ask a friend to confirm anything you read online

quizzes.question: Which activity does this chapter ask you to do before the mechanics?
options: Build a payment channel on your own computer
Watch a video explaining how Lightning works
Read the Lightning source code line by line

quizzes.question: Once a Lightning channel is open, how are the payments between the two people sent?
options: Each one waits for a block on the base blockchain
Each one is approved by a bank before it is sent
Near-instantly and almost free, off the main chain

quizzes.question: What do the 'flavors' of Lightning wallet depend on?
options: Which phone brand the app is for
Who holds the keys and the channels
How many merchants accept the wallet

quizzes.question: What does a custodial Lightning wallet ask of you, compared with self-custody?
options: Managing your own channels and keys by yourself
Running your own full node at home all the time
Trusting a provider to run the channels for you

quizzes.question: What does open-source Lightning wallet software let the community do?
options: Check that the code does what it claims
Change anyone's balance if enough people agree
Reverse a payment made by mistake

quizzes.question: Why do many people begin with a custodial Lightning wallet?
options: It gives them full control over their own channels
It never needs a phone or an internet connection
Setup takes minutes and needs little technical work

quizzes.question: How long does a typical Lightning payment take to settle?
options: Under a single second
About ten minutes
About a full day

quizzes.question: Where does this section say Bitcoin stops being theoretical?
options: In a classroom, when you read about it
At the till, when you pay for things
On an exchange, when you trade it

quizzes.question: What do shoppers do at checkout when a store accepts Lightning through a plugin?
options: Scan a QR code instead of typing card details
Type a long recovery phrase into the website
Wait for the bank to approve the whole purchase

quizzes.question: How is the EkasiPay network described in this section?
options: A plan that will only start in a few years' time
Something happening at shops you can walk to
An example copied from a city far away from here

quizzes.question: What do bitcoin-linked gift cards and prepaid cards help people do?
options: Avoid ever using bitcoin in any form whatsoever
Skip learning anything about wallets altogether
Ease from familiar payments into Lightning

quizzes.question: What does it mean for the circle to be 'strengthened' in a circular economy?
options: Each person cashes out to rand as fast as possible
Each new merchant and local spender adds to it
Each shop stops taking any bitcoin payments

quizzes.question: What does this chapter say will make you a more confident Bitcoin user?
options: Learning to write programs in several languages
Buying more bitcoin as often as you can
Understanding how it works under the hood

quizzes.question: What is the public key used for, according to this section?
options: Receiving funds, and it can be shared openly
Proving ownership, and it must be kept secret
Mining new blocks, and it is kept offline

quizzes.question: Which direction does the link between the private and public key work in?
options: Both: either key can be worked out from the other
Neither: the two keys are chosen independently
One way: the public key comes from the private

quizzes.question: What happens to a hash if you change just one letter of the input?
options: It becomes a completely different string
It changes only in the last few characters
It stays exactly the same as before

quizzes.question: What happens to the leftover amount when you spend a UTXO?
options: It is kept by the miner as an additional fee
It comes back to you as change in a new UTXO
It disappears from the whole network for good

quizzes.question: Which of the two roles proposes new blocks of transactions?
options: Miners
Nodes
Developers

quizzes.question: What does a full node download and check for itself?
options: Only the transactions that its own owner makes
Every transaction and block, to check the rules
Only the very newest block, checked once each day

quizzes.question: What does the network's difficulty adjustment keep steady?
options: About one new miner every ten days or so
About one new rule every ten weeks or so
About one new block every ten minutes

quizzes.question: Which transactions tend to be picked up first when the mempool is busy?
options: Those that were sent the longest ago
Those offering higher fees
Those with the smallest amounts

quizzes.question: Who checks that a new block follows every rule, according to this section?
options: Only the miner who built it
A bank chosen by the network
Every node, independently
